doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Advice for young trumpet players
summary: He urges versatility, classical basics, transcribing solos, and learning Pro Tools, noting he records solos at home.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well the business has changed a lot so just to wrap up, do you have any advice for the young trumpet player out there who wants to do what you did?

Yes I do actually. If you want to have something you can have it. So if you want to be a trumpet player for a living you can do that. There’s room for great players and there always will be. So a student trumpet player that wants to become a studio musician or play jazz and make records and things like that they can do that. It’s up to them, entirely up to them. But there’s always room, there’s always going to be jazz around, there’s always going to be records being done, there’s always going to be music period. But they need to learn to be a versatile player. You can’t just do one style you know. You should be able to play a classical piece you know, not necessarily a principal trumpet player in an orchestra, but be able to approach it properly. And a lot of that is mental and knowing how to attack the notes and where to breathe properly. That’s what has to do with classical music, there’s a politic. There’s a lot of things that you need to do. Now that is necessary. That’s the basis. Now you’ve learned how to walk. Now you need to learn how to jog and then you learn other stuff. And then listening to records and listening to everybody playing. Pick-up, pick their brains by records. Because you’re not going to be able to do it live, like I had the opportunity to do. Let them listen and pick the brains on records of everybody’s playing. Learn that. Play along with it. Learn it. Transcribe it, it’s wonderful. Transcribe the solo. When you transcribe it then you really know it and then you can look at it and study it and say oh okay, and look at the chord changes and see what you did to the chord change, you know? And once again all styles, Dixieland, like I said you know bebop, mainstream, you name it. It all needs to be done but you have to be versatile. And also these days you need to know how to use Pro Tools and all that kind of stuff because they’re going to be asked to do that ‘cause that’s the way it is and it’s not going to go away. So if they want to do that they should have that in their — they should

have that in their file that they can do that. Because they’ll be called to do a solo and you’ll do it at home in your room and you put the solo and you fly it to them and they’ve got your solo. I do that.
If they ask for a solo I just do a solo and send it to them you know because it’s easier than traveling these days and it’s a lot cheaper for them not to fly me somewhere.
